Title: A Latin-script name of ordinary length is accepted
Steps: 1. Type Jean into the Votre prenom field
Expected result: The field is accepted with no error
Actual result: No error is shown

Title: A three-character name, a real French given name
Steps: 1. Type Luc
Expected result: The name is accepted: three characters is a valid name
Actual result: “First Name must be at least 4 characters”

Title: A name exactly on the lower boundary — four characters
Steps: 1. Type Jean
Expected result: Accepted
Actual result: Accepted

Title: A name exactly on the upper boundary — 28 characters
Precondition: The form is open in Chrome
Steps: 1. Type a string of 28 Latin letters
Expected result: Accepted, and the limit message agrees with the actual boundary
Actual result: Accepted, but at 29 characters the message reads “less than 28”

Title: A name one character past the boundary — 29 characters
Precondition: The form is open in Chrome
Steps: 1. Type a string of 29 Latin letters
Expected result: Rejected
Actual result: Rejected

Title: The name length limit differs between browsers
Steps:
1. Type a 30-character name in Chrome
2. Spoof the user agent as Firefox and retype the same value
Expected result: Identical behaviour in both browsers
Actual result: Chrome rejects it; with a Firefox user agent the same 30 characters are accepted

Title: A name with French diacritics
Steps:
1. Type François
2. Type Amélie
Expected result: Both accepted: the interface is French
Actual result: Both rejected with “Please enter a valid first name”

Title: A name in a non-Latin script
Steps:
1. Type Жанна into the form
2. Send the same value directly to the API
Expected result: Support for non-Latin scripts is a deliberate decision applied identically on both layers
Actual result: The form rejects it; the server accepts and stores the same value

Title: A name containing digits
Steps: 1. Type Jean2
Expected result: Rejected
Actual result: Rejected

Title: A name with a hyphen and an apostrophe
Steps:
1. Type Jean-Paul
2. Type O'Brien
Expected result: Both accepted
Actual result: Both accepted

Title: A name consisting only of spaces
Steps:
1. Type four spaces into the name field
2. Send the same value to the API
Expected result: Rejected as an empty value
Actual result: Accepted by the form; the server answers 201 for the same value

Title: Spaces around a name are not trimmed
Steps: 1. Type “   Jean   ”
Expected result: The value is trimmed before submission
Actual result: Accepted and sent to the server with its spaces

Title: A name made of emoji
Steps:
1. Paste emoji into the name field
2. Send the same value to the API
Expected result: Rejected on both layers
Actual result: The form rejects it; the server accepts and stores it

Title: Pasting an over-long value from the clipboard
Precondition: The clipboard holds a string longer than the limit
Steps: 1. Paste the string into the name field with a keyboard shortcut
Expected result: Input is capped at the field level, or an error appears immediately
Actual result: There is no maxlength attribute; the limit is discovered only from the message

Title: The error text of the last-name field
Steps: 1. Type a value with a disallowed character into the Votre nom field
Expected result: The message refers to the last name
Actual result: “Please enter a valid first name”

Title: Last-name length boundaries at 4 and 28
Steps: 1. Type 3, then 4, then 28, then 29 characters
Expected result: Rejected, accepted, accepted, rejected
Actual result: The boundaries hold; the texts are off by one, as in TC-FV-004

Title: Asymmetric limits between first and last name
Precondition: The form is open in a non-Chrome browser
Steps:
1. Type 30 characters into the first name
2. Type 30 characters into the last name
Expected result: Both fields behave identically
Actual result: The first name accepts 30 characters, the last name rejects them: only the first name branches on the user agent

Title: A phone number one digit below the boundary — 7 digits
Precondition: The form has been reloaded and Backspace has not been pressed in the field
Expected result: Rejected
Actual result: “Phone Number must be at least 8 characters”

Title: A phone number exactly on the lower boundary — 8 digits
Precondition: The form has been reloaded and Backspace has not been pressed in the field
Expected result: Accepted
Actual result: Accepted

Title: A phone number at the upper boundary — 16 and 17 digits
Steps:
1. Type 16 digits
2. Type 17 digits
Expected result: Accepted, then rejected, with the message matching the boundary
Actual result: Accepted then rejected; the text is again off by one

Title: Backspace irreversibly removes the phone minimum length
Steps:
1. Type two digits — the minimum-length error appears
2. Press Backspace
3. Type one more digit
Expected result: The minimum-length error stays while there are fewer than eight digits
Actual result: At the value 121 the error disappears: minLength was reset to 0 and never restored

Title: A phone number in international format
Expected result: Accepted or normalised
Actual result: Rejected with “Ce champ est requis” — the field is filled in, yet the message claims it is required

Title: A phone number in the national French format with spaces
Expected result: Accepted or normalised
Actual result: Rejected with the same incorrect message

Title: A phone number of nothing but zeroes
Expected result: Rejected as obviously not a number, or accepted deliberately
Actual result: Accepted: neither layer performs a meaningful number check

Title: A phone number in Arabic-Indic digits
Expected result: Rejected
Actual result: Rejected

Title: The phone field type on a mobile device
Precondition: The form is open at a width of 375 px
Steps: 1. Tap the phone field
Expected result: The numeric keyboard opens
Actual result: The field type is text instead of tel, so the standard keyboard opens

Title: The error text for an invalid phone format
Steps:
1. Type +33612345678 into the Numéro de téléphone field
2. Read the error text below the field
Expected result: The message describes the expected number format
Actual result: “Ce champ est requis” — a required-field message on a field that is filled in

Title: A valid email address
Steps:
1. Type a@b.co
2. Type jean.dupont@mail.example.co.uk
Expected result: Both accepted
Actual result: Both accepted

Title: An address with no top-level domain
Steps: 1. Type a@b
Expected result: Rejected
Actual result: Rejected

Title: A one-character top-level domain
Steps: 1. Type a@b.c
Expected result: Rejected
Actual result: Rejected

Title: A domain beginning with a hyphen
Steps: 1. Type a@-b.co
Expected result: Rejected: such a domain cannot exist
Actual result: Accepted by both layers

Title: An address with an IP literal as the domain
Expected result: Rejected for a consumer form
Actual result: Accepted by both layers

Title: An address with a trailing space, the typical paste case
Steps: 1. Paste “a@b.co ” with a trailing space
Expected result: The space is trimmed and the address is accepted
Actual result: Rejected, and the user cannot see why

Title: An internationalised address
Steps: 1. Type жан@почта.рф
Expected result: Behaviour is defined and identical on both layers
Actual result: Rejected by the form, and the server expression rejects it too — no mismatch, but no support either

Title: An upper-case address duplicating an existing one
Precondition: The user a@b.co is already registered
Steps: 1. Register A@B.CO
Expected result: The address is lower-cased and rejected as a duplicate
Actual result: Accepted: there is no normalisation and no uniqueness

Title: The email field type
Steps: 1. Inspect the type attribute of the Votre email field
Expected result: type is email
Actual result: type is text

Title: A password at the lower length boundary
Steps:
1. Type Abcdef1 — seven characters
2. Type Abcdef1! — eight characters
Expected result: Rejected, then accepted
Actual result: Rejected, then accepted

Title: A password at the upper length boundary
Steps:
1. Type 28 characters
2. Type 29 characters
3. Send a 1000-character password directly to the API
Expected result: Accepted, then rejected, with the same boundary enforced server-side
Actual result: The form enforces the boundary; the server accepts a 1000-character password

Title: A password valid on the client and invalid on the server
Precondition: The form is open and the server is reachable
Steps:
1. Type password1 into both password fields
2. Fill the remaining fields validly and submit
Expected result: The form rejects the password before submission, or surfaces the server error
Actual result: The form accepts it, the server answers 400, the user sees the success screen, and nothing is stored

Title: A password with no lower-case letters, against a message demanding them
Steps: 1. Type 27 upper-case letters followed by a digit
Expected result: Behaviour matches the message text
Actual result: Accepted, even though the message demands a lower-case letter

Title: A password invalid on the client and valid on the server
Steps:
1. Type Abcdef1^ into the password field
2. Send the same value directly to the API
Expected result: The accepted special-character sets match on both layers
Actual result: The form rejects it; the same password is accepted by the API with 201

Title: A password containing a space
Steps: 1. Type Abcdef1 2
Expected result: Behaviour is defined and explained by the message
Actual result: Rejected, but the message says nothing about spaces

Title: A password with non-Latin characters
Steps:
1. Type Пароль123
2. Type Abcdef1é
Expected result: Passphrases in the user's own language are supported
Actual result: Both rejected: the character set is limited to Latin letters and eight special characters

Title: The message never mentions the special-character requirement
Steps:
1. Type Abcdef12 — a password with no special character
2. Submit the form
Expected result: The user is told a special character is required
Actual result: The form accepts it, the server answers 400, and the requirement is shown nowhere

Title: The password visibility toggle with a mouse
Precondition: The password field holds a value
Steps:
1. Click the eye icon
2. Click it again
Expected result: The password is revealed and hidden again
Actual result: Works on a mouse click

Title: A weak but formally valid password
Steps: 1. Type Abcdef1! — a password near the top of breach dictionaries
Expected result: A strength warning is shown, or the password is rejected
Actual result: Accepted without comment; there is no strength indicator

Title: Password manager behaviour
Precondition: The browser password manager is enabled
Steps: 1. Open the form and try to generate a password
Expected result: The manager recognises the field as a new password
Actual result: No field carries an autocomplete attribute, so recognition never happens

Title: A non-matching password confirmation
Steps: 1. Type different values into the password and confirmation fields
Expected result: A mismatch error is shown
Actual result: “The passwords do not match”

Title: Changing the password after a successful confirmation
Precondition: Both password fields hold the same value and the form is valid
Steps:
1. Edit the main password field only
2. Inspect the confirmation field and the button
Expected result: A mismatch error appears
Actual result: No error appears and the button silently goes disabled — a dead end

Title: The rules applied to the confirmation field
Steps: 1. Type the same value into both fields, one that violates the password character set
Expected result: Both fields apply the same set of rules
Actual result: The confirmation has no character-set check, only length and equality

Title: Submitting without accepting the terms
Precondition: Every field holds a valid value
Steps:
1. Leave the consent checkbox unticked
2. Try to submit
Expected result: Submission is blocked
Actual result: The button is disabled and nothing is sent

Title: Clicking the consent text
Steps: 1. Click the text “J'ai lu et accepté…”
Expected result: The checkbox toggles
Actual result: It does not: the text is not tied to the field by a label

Title: The error text on the consent checkbox
Precondition: The form is filled in and the box is unticked
Steps: 1. Trigger validation on the checkbox
Expected result: An explanation of why the form will not submit is shown
Actual result: The error block is empty: the rule carries no message

Title: A stray asterisk above the checkbox
Steps: 1. Look at the area between the password confirmation and the checkbox
Expected result: No stray characters
Actual result: A lone red asterisk with no caption

Title: The server answers with an error and the form shows success
Precondition: The server is reachable; the password is valid on the client and invalid on the server
Steps:
1. Fill the form with the password password1
2. Submit
3. Inspect the screen and the users table
Expected result: An error is shown, the user stays on the form, and the data is preserved
Actual result: POST 400, the screen reads “Thank you for subscription!”, and the table holds 0 rows

Title: The server is unreachable and the form shows success
Steps:
1. Fill the form with valid values
2. Submit
Expected result: A connection error is shown with an option to retry
Actual result: ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED in the console, success on screen

Title: Rapid repeated presses of the submit button
Precondition: The form is valid and the database is empty
Steps: 1. Press the submit button three times in a row
Expected result: Exactly one record is created
Actual result: Three requests, three 201 responses, three identical rows

Title: Feedback while the submission is in flight
Steps: 1. Submit the form and watch the button
Expected result: The button enters a pending state
Actual result: There is no pending state; the button stays active until the success screen appears

Title: Submitting the form with the Enter key
Precondition: The form is valid and focus is in a text field
Steps: 1. Press Enter
Expected result: The form submits and behaves exactly as a button press would

Title: The form reset runs after navigating away
Steps:
1. Submit the form
2. Check the console for React warnings
Expected result: No warnings about updating state on an unmounted component

Title: Going back from the success screen
Precondition: The form has been submitted and the success screen is open
Steps: 1. Press the browser back button
Expected result: The user returns to the form in a sensible state

Title: The contents of the submitted request body
Steps:
1. Submit the form
2. Inspect the request body in the network panel
Expected result: Only the fields the server needs are sent; the password confirmation is not

Title: No request timeout is configured
Precondition: The server accepts the connection but never answers
Steps:
1. Submit the form
2. Watch the request state in the network panel
Expected result: The request aborts on a timeout with a clear message
Actual result: The axios configuration sets no timeout, so the request hangs indefinitely while the user is already on the success screen

Title: The API address variable is not set
Steps:
1. Build and open the frontend
2. Submit the form
Expected result: A clear configuration error

Title: Retrying after a failed submission
Precondition: The submission ended with a server error
Steps: 1. Try to correct the data and submit again
Expected result: The user stays on the form with the entered data preserved
Actual result: The user has already been moved to the success screen and the form was reset — retrying is impossible

Title: Layout at a width of 375 px
Steps:
1. Set the window width to 375 px
2. Inspect the Votre nom field
Expected result: Every field fits inside the card
Actual result: The 400-px last-name field spills outside the card and off the screen

Title: Layout at a width of 320 px
Steps: 1. Set the window width to 320 px
Expected result: No horizontal scrolling and the content stays readable

Title: Card behaviour at intermediate resolutions
Steps: 1. Check 768, 1024 and 1440 px
Expected result: The card width changes predictably

Title: The appearance of the disabled submit button
Steps: 1. Inspect the button and hover over it
Expected result: The disabled state is visible
Actual result: Colour and opacity match the enabled state and the hover effect still works

Title: The font class used in the form markup
Steps: 1. Search the built CSS for font-OpenSans
Expected result: The class is present and sets a family
Actual result: The class is never generated: the Tailwind config has no fontFamily section

Title: The social sign-up block
Steps: 1. Look for the Google and Facebook buttons
Expected result: Either the block is rendered or the code is deleted
Actual result: The component exists but is wired into no screen — the page holds one button

Title: The link for existing users
Steps: 1. Click the text “Vous avez déjà un compte?”
Expected result: Navigation to sign-in
Actual result: The text is not a link and leads nowhere

Title: A typo in the confirm-password caption
Steps: 1. Read the caption of the sixth field
Expected result: Correct French text
Actual result: “Confirmez vorte mot de passe” instead of votre

Title: The tab title and favicon
Steps: 1. Look at the browser tab title
Expected result: The product name
Actual result: “React App” and the stock create-react-app icon

Title: Filled-field indication
Steps:
1. Fill a field without moving focus away
2. Move focus away
Expected result: The field state updates immediately

Title: Zooming the page to 200 percent
Steps: 1. Zoom the browser to 200 percent
Expected result: Nothing is clipped and every field stays reachable

Title: The operating system dark theme
Precondition: The system is set to dark mode
Steps: 1. Open the form
Expected result: The design deliberately supports or ignores the theme

Title: Accessible names for the form fields
Steps: 1. Check every field for label, id and aria-label
Expected result: Every field has an accessible name

Title: Completing the form with the keyboard alone
Steps:
1. Tab through every element
2. Try to reveal the password from the keyboard
Expected result: Every interactive element is reachable
Actual result: The password toggle is a plain div with no tabindex or role, and only eight elements are reachable

Title: Visibility of the focus indicator
Steps: 1. Tab through the fields and watch the outline
Expected result: The focused field is unmistakable

Title: Contrast of the field captions
Steps: 1. Measure the contrast of captions and error text against the background
Expected result: Contrast of at least 4.5 to 1

Title: Association between error messages and fields
Steps: 1. Trigger an error and check aria-describedby and role
Expected result: The error is tied to its field and announced by assistive technology

Title: Document language and message language
Steps:
1. Check the lang attribute
2. Trigger errors in different fields
Expected result: The document language matches the interface, and messages share one language
Actual result: lang="en" on a French interface, with messages mixed between French and English

Title: Conveying that fields are required
Steps: 1. Listen to the fields with a screen reader
Expected result: The requirement is conveyed by an attribute, not by an asterisk alone

Title: Language consistency of messages within the form
Steps:
1. Trigger an error in the name field
2. Trigger a format error in the phone field
3. Compare the languages of the two messages
Expected result: Every interface text is in one language

Title: Opening a route that does not exist
Steps: 1. Open /nonexistent-page-404
Expected result: A 404 page or a redirect to the form
Actual result: A completely blank page with an empty root element

Title: Opening the success screen directly
Steps: 1. Open /success
Expected result: A redirect to the form
Actual result: The thank-you screen is shown with no registration

Title: The back button on the success screen
Steps: 1. Press “Go back”
Expected result: Return to the form
Actual result: Navigation to the form works

Title: Reloading the page on a nested route
Steps: 1. Reload the page
Expected result: The route opens with no 404 from the server

Title: Creating a user with a valid request body
Precondition: The server and database are running
Steps: 1. Send POST /users/create with every field valid
Expected result: 201, no password in the response, one row in the database
Actual result: 201, no password in the response, and the row was created

Title: A request body without a first name
Steps: 1. Send a body with no first_name key
Expected result: 400 naming the field
Actual result: 500 Internal server error — the request reaches the insert and fails on NOT NULL

Title: A request body without a last name
Steps: 1. Send a body with no last_name key
Expected result: 400 naming the field
Actual result: 500 Internal server error

Title: A request body without an email address
Steps: 1. Send a body with no email key
Actual result: 400 “ERROR: invalid email”

Title: A request body without consent
Steps: 1. Send a body with no is_agree key
Actual result: 400 “ERROR: is_agree not checked”

Title: An empty object as the request body
Steps: 1. Send {}
Expected result: 400 listing the missing fields
Actual result: 400, but the message names only is_agree and omits the rest

Title: Consent sent as the string “false”
Steps: 1. Send "is_agree":"false"
Expected result: 400: consent must be the boolean true
Actual result: 201 — the string counts as truthy

Title: Consent sent as a number
Steps: 1. Send "is_agree":1

Title: The first name sent as a number
Steps: 1. Send "first_name":12345
Actual result: 201, and 12345 is stored in the database

Title: The first name sent as an array
Steps: 1. Send "first_name":["a","b"]
Actual result: 201, and {"a","b"} is stored in the database

Title: The phone number sent as a number
Steps: 1. Send "phone_number":79001234567
Expected result: 400, or an explicit type conversion
Actual result: 201: the regular expression check coerces the number to a string implicitly

Title: Unknown fields in the request body
Steps: 1. Add a role field with the value admin to the body
Expected result: The field is dropped or the request is rejected
Actual result: 201, and the field is echoed back in the response

Title: Response conformance to the declared contract
Steps: 1. Create a user and compare the response with ShowUserDto
Expected result: The response holds exactly the four declared fields
Actual result: The response carries id and is_agree beyond the contract

Title: Malformed JSON in the request body
Steps: 1. Send {oops
Expected result: 400 with no internal detail disclosed
Actual result: 400 carrying the parser text “Unexpected token o in JSON at position 1”

Title: A request without a content type header
Steps: 1. Send the form as application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Expected result: 415, or the body is parsed correctly
Actual result: 400 “is_agree not checked” — the body is simply not parsed and the reason is not stated

Title: Request body size boundaries
Steps:
1. Send a 92 KB body
2. Send a 204 KB body
Expected result: Both rejected by an application-level field length check
Actual result: 92 KB → 201 and a row is written; 204 KB → 413 from the Express default

Title: The service root route
Steps: 1. Send GET /
Expected result: 200 “Service is working!”, as declared in the code and in the e2e test
Actual result: 404: AppController is not registered with AppModule

Title: Unsupported routes and methods
Steps:
1. GET /users/create
2. PUT /users/create
3. GET /users
Actual result: All three answer 404

Title: A ten-thousand-character name
Steps: 1. Send a first_name of 10,000 characters
Expected result: 400: the length is bounded
Actual result: 201, and the value is stored in full — the column is declared without a length limit

Title: A name consisting of a single space
Steps: 1. Send "first_name":" "
Expected result: 400: the value is empty once trimmed
Actual result: 201 — the check tests truthiness, and a space is truthy

Title: A password with no upper length bound
Steps: 1. Send a 1000-character password
Expected result: 400: the same 28-character boundary as the client
Actual result: 201 — the server expression sets no upper bound

Title: A one-digit phone number
Steps: 1. Send "phone_number":"7"
Expected result: 400: a minimum of eight digits, as on the client
Actual result: 201 — the server checks only the character set

Title: An email address longer than the standard allows
Steps: 1. Send an address longer than 320 characters

Title: Fields carrying null
Steps: 1. Send "first_name":null

Title: Duplicate keys in the JSON body
Steps: 1. Send a body with two email keys
Expected result: The behaviour is defined and documented

Title: Null bytes and control characters in values
Steps: 1. Send a name containing \u0000
Expected result: 400, or safe handling

Title: An injected identifier overwrites another user's record
Precondition: The database holds a user with a known id
Steps:
1. Send a registration with the "id" of an existing row added to the body
2. Read that row back
Expected result: The id field is ignored and a new record is created
Actual result: The response is 201, yet row id=2 was replaced: Jean/a@b.co became ATTACKER/attacker@evil.co

Title: How the password is stored
Steps: 1. Read the password column
Expected result: An irreversible hash is stored
Actual result: The original string Abcdef1! is stored

Title: The password in the application log
Precondition: The stack was started with the README command, so DEBUG is true
Steps:
1. Send a registration
2. Read the backend container log
Expected result: The password never reaches the log under any configuration
Actual result: The request body is printed in full, password included

Title: Registration rate limiting
Steps: 1. Send sixty requests in a row
Expected result: Some requests are rejected with 429
Actual result: 60 out of 60 succeed in 0.94 seconds

Title: The cross-origin sharing policy
Steps: 1. Send a preflight and then a main request with a foreign Origin
Expected result: Only the application's own frontend origin is allowed
Actual result: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and a successful 201 from a foreign origin

Title: SQL injection through the form fields
Steps:
1. Send a name containing a closing quote and DROP TABLE
2. Verify the table still exists
Expected result: The query is parameterised and the table is intact
Actual result: The value is stored as plain text and the table is intact — TypeORM parameterises its queries

Title: Storing potentially executable markup
Steps: 1. Send a script tag as the first name
Expected result: The value is rejected or escaped on write
Actual result: Stored verbatim. There is no direct exploit today because no endpoint reads it back — the risk is deferred

Title: Security headers in the response
Steps: 1. Inspect the response headers
Expected result: CSP, X-Content-Type-Options and X-Frame-Options are present
Actual result: Not one security header is present

Title: Disclosure of the framework in use
Steps: 1. Inspect the X-Powered-By header
Expected result: The header is absent
Actual result: X-Powered-By: Express

Title: Sending the password over an unencrypted channel
Precondition: The stack was started per the instructions
Steps: 1. Inspect the scheme the frontend uses to reach the API
Expected result: The traffic is protected by TLS
Actual result: The exchange runs over http and the password travels in clear text

Title: External reachability of the database
Steps: 1. Inspect the published ports
Expected result: The database is not published externally
Actual result: 5432 is published on 0.0.0.0 and the password is hard-coded as secret in the config file

Title: Confirming ownership of the email address
Steps: 1. Register with an address that is knowingly not yours
Expected result: The account stays inactive until confirmed
Actual result: The record is created immediately, with no confirmation and no captcha

Title: Internal detail disclosure in a 500 response
Steps: 1. Trigger a 500 with a request that omits the first name
Expected result: The client receives no stack trace
Actual result: Only “Internal server error” is returned; the trace stays in the log

Title: Prototype pollution through the request body
Steps: 1. Send a body containing a __proto__ key
Expected result: The key is ignored

Title: Uniqueness of the email address
Steps: 1. Send the same registration twice with one address
Expected result: The second request is rejected with 409
Actual result: Both requests succeed and the database holds two rows with the same address

Title: Column length constraints
Steps: 1. Inspect the users table definition
Expected result: The text columns carry a maximum length
Actual result: Every column is declared character varying with no length

Title: Automatic schema synchronisation
Steps: 1. Inspect ormconfig.ts
Expected result: The schema is driven by migrations
Actual result: synchronize: true — the schema is aligned to the entities on every start

Title: Record timestamps
Steps: 1. Inspect the columns of the users table
Expected result: Creation and modification marks are present
Actual result: There is no created_at and no updated_at

Title: Sequence consumption on failed inserts
Steps:
1. Send two requests that produce a 500
2. Create a valid user
Expected result: Identifiers run consecutively
Actual result: After two failures the successful record received id 5 instead of 3

Title: Data survival across a stack restart
Steps:
1. Run docker compose down
2. Bring the stack back up
3. Read the users table
Expected result: The data is still there
Actual result: The volume is mounted at /var/lib/mysql while Postgres writes to /var/lib/postgresql/data — the data is lost

Title: Table indexes
Steps: 1. Inspect the indexes on the users table
Expected result: An index exists on the field sign-in will search by
Actual result: The primary key is the only index

Title: Storing diacritics in the database
Steps:
1. Send the name François through the API, bypassing the frontend
2. Read the value back
Expected result: The value is stored and read without corruption
Actual result: Stored and read correctly

Precondition: A clean clone of the repository with Docker installed
